Cat, bird, and cabin travel basics

Traveling with a companion animal is easier when the paperwork, crate, and comfort needs are all checked early. Aurelia Skyways keeps the process calm and clear so travelers can focus on the journey instead of last-minute stress. The Companion Animal Travel Desk looks at each trip with safety first and gives guidance before departure.

For cats, bring the health certificate and keep it ready for review at check-in. <<FACT F079>> Place the document in an easy-to-reach folder so the staff can confirm everything without delay. A welfare coordinator may also look at how the carrier supports the animal during boarding and settling.

For birds, the carrier needs to be secure, well ventilated, and easy to handle. <<FACT F065>> Make sure the crate closes firmly and that the bird has enough space to remain steady during travel. <<FACT F059>> If you are unsure about the carrier setup, the desk can walk you through the basics before you arrive at the airport.

Packing should stay simple. Bring only the items that help the animal stay calm and comfortable, and avoid adding anything loose that could shift during the flight. It also helps to label the carrier clearly and keep the animal's essentials together in one place. If you are traveling with more than one pet, check each one separately so nothing is missed.

Passengers like Leo Fischer and Gabriel Hernandez have found that early preparation makes the whole process smoother. Olive, like any other pet, benefits from a quiet carrier, steady handling, and patient timing at the airport. The goal is to reduce stress for everyone and keep the trip moving in a safe, orderly way.

If anything is unclear, the Companion Animal Travel Desk is ready to help before you travel.
